key_insight: HiMuon replaces full-matrix Muon updates with independent Newton-Schulz updates on small tiles, preserving local spectral structure while cutting update cost.
engineering_relevance: The method enables faster, more GPU-friendly optimizer steps through tiled kernels, batching, and chunked execution for large neural-network weights.
method: Partition each momentum-gradient matrix into T×T tiles.
Apply the same finite Newton-Schulz map independently to each tile.
Reassemble the tiled outputs; optionally use tile-size schedules and cross-layer batching.
evidence_signal: The paper reports transformer-training experiments and controlled matrix-function diagnostics showing improved optimizer-step efficiency while staying close to full-matrix Muon in tested regimes.
watch_item: Because HiMuon is a local tile-wise map rather than a convergent approximation to the full update, cross-tile spectral interactions are discarded and performance may depend on tile size.
paper_title: Hierarchical Muon: Tiled Newton-Schulz Updates for Efficient Muon Optimization
